A wooden cage sits crooked beside the trail. Inside, a man in a torn merchant's coat grips the bars. "Goblins," he rasps. "They took my wife and my boy into the woods. Please. Their Gatekeeper carries the key."
The merchant is still in his cage. "You came back," he says, and his voice cracks.
{hero} braces against the bars and heaves. The wood splinters with a crack that echoes through the trees. Somewhere close, two goblin voices shout and come running.
The lock gives a sharp snap, and the pick with it. Two goblin guards burst out of the brush, blades drawn.
{hero} works the lock in silence. A soft click, and the door swings open.
The Gatekeeper's iron key turns in the lock, and the door swings open.
The merchant presses a few coins into {hero}'s hand. "They went east, past the Gatekeeper's post. Find my family. I'll wait at the trail."
The trail sinks into black, still water. The only way on is through it.
{hero} sees the ripples a heartbeat early. "Back!" A giant crocodile bursts from the murk, and the party is ready for it.
The water explodes. A giant crocodile lunges at the party before anyone sees it coming.
In the beast's gullet, among the bones, the party finds a pouch of coins and an unbroken potion.
A shallow cave ringed with fresh bones. Low snarls echo from inside.
Go in and take the den
{hero} roars and bangs steel on stone. The wolves bolt into the forest, leaving their scraps behind.
The pack lies still. Among the bones are a dead traveller's coins and a potion.
A mossy altar to some forgotten god of the wild. Faded carvings circle its base.
Read the rite in the carvings
{hero} traces the carvings and speaks the old words in the right order.
A warm wind stirs the leaves. The forest feels sharper, every sound clearer.
The moss darkens and the air goes cold. Whatever lives here did not like that prayer. The party's arms feel heavy.
A deep mud pit swallows the trail.
{hero} sets the pace and the party grinds through without breaking stride.
{hero} spots a line of roots under the surface. The party crosses with dry boots.
Waist-deep, one heavy step at a time. Everyone comes out the far side exhausted.
The detour takes hours through thorns and bramble. The party's legs are slow for a while.
A ransacked camp: torn tents, a cold fire pit, and supplies scattered in the dirt.
{hero} spots a snare hidden under a bedroll and springs it with a stick.
A hidden snare snaps shut. Someone takes a nasty cut.
There's enough left to pack up and carry, or the fire pit could be rekindled to make a safe place to rest.
Under the tents are a few coins and a potion.
A fortified guard post blocks the only path east. A goblin captain barks orders at his squad. On his belt hangs a heavy iron key.
Study the defences for a weak point
{hero} spots a gap in the palisade where the logs have rotted. The party slips through and strikes before the squad can form up.
"Supplies from the Chief!" {hero} calls, and the outer guard waves them in. One goblin less to fight, and the rest are caught off guard.
The captain falls, and his iron key with him. Beyond the post, the path leads deeper into goblin land.
A woman's scream cuts through the trees. "Help! They've taken my boy, they're going to eat him!" She stumbles toward the party from the brush.
Hold back and watch the brush
{hero} catches the glint of a blade in the brush. It's an ambush! The party draws steel before the raiders can spring it.
Goblin raiders burst from the brush on every side. It was bait!
The woman's face lights up when she hears about the caged merchant. "My husband! You freed him!" She presses her last potions into the party's hands. "The fortress is east. Bring my boy home."
The woman, shaking, explains that the goblins were using her as bait. "My husband is caged somewhere near the forest edge, and my son is in their fortress to the east."
The path narrows between two steep banks. It's quiet. Too quiet.
{hero} stops the party. A wire, barely visible, runs across the path to a stack of spiked logs above.
Disarm it and salvage the spikes
One by one, the party steps over the wire and leaves it behind.
{hero} cuts the wire and pries the iron spikes out of the logs. They'll make good throwing weapons.
The wire snaps. Spiked logs roll down the bank and catch {hero}, leaving a deep, bleeding gash. A goblin patrol comes to check its trap.
The patrol is dealt with. The path ahead is clear.
A crude lookout platform rises above the trees. From up there, you could see the whole valley.
Talk or sneak your way up
{hero} walks up the ladder like they belong there. The lookouts never think to ask.
From the platform the party can see the goblin fortress to the east, a boar rooting in the grove, and figures moving in the marsh. A lookout's purse lies forgotten on the boards.
A rope snare dangles over the path, set by someone who knows the trade.
Reset the snare for its catch
Cut it down for the catch
{hero} reads the knife marks on the trees and follows them to the poacher's hidden stash.
The snare holds a fat marsh hare and, tied to the line, a poacher's spare potion and a few coins.
The rope whips free and knocks a purse into the bog. The splash brings scavengers running.
The scavengers are gone, and so is the purse.
An enraged boar paws the ground at the edge of its feeding ground, tusks low.
"Steady!" {hero} holds the line as the boar thunders in, and the party meets it with steel.
That night the party roasts the boar over a small fire. A good meal does wonders.
A carved monolith hums with old warding magic. The runes glow faintly blue.
{hero} presses both hands to the stone. Its power floods in, bright and cold, and lingers.
{hero} hums along with the stone until their minds meet. The party's Mana swells.
The runes are a boundary marker, and a map: a chapel to the north-east is still warded and safe.
A gentle pulse runs up the party's arms. Their Mana stirs.
The stone pulls instead of giving. The party feels their magic seeping away.
A friendly hermit sorts herbs on a flat rock. "Field medicine, if you can pay for it. Twenty-five gold to set up my kit."
Help her identify the rare herbs
{hero} names three herbs she's never seen. She laughs. "Keep your gold, scholar."
She unpacks her kettles and vials. Her Alchemist Station is open for business.
A barricaded goblin fortress. Smoke rises from a great cookpot in the middle, and a child's cry carries over the walls.
{hero} leads the party in under a cartload of firewood. Nobody checks.
{hero} cuts the barricade's lashings. It collapses onto the Chief's guard, and the party charges through the gap.
The party charges the gate. The outer patrol rushes out to meet them.
The patrol is down, and the way into the fortress is open.
In the middle of the camp, the Goblin Chief is shoving a small boy toward the bubbling pot. He turns, roaring.
The boy runs into his mother's arms, and his father is waiting at the trail. The whole family is together again. They empty their hidden savings into the party's hands.
The party brings the boy back to his father at the forest edge. His mother is still missing, but the merchant swears he'll find her, and pays the party what he can.
The boy's mother weeps as she holds him. His father is still caged somewhere, she says, but she'll find him now. She pays the party what she can.
The boy is safe, but alone. The party takes him toward the forest edge to look for his family. He gives them the few coins in his pocket.
